 Pa. residents can get up to $2,000 in heating assistance. How to apply 
 Pennsylvania's LIHEAP program is accepting applications through April 23, 2027, but officials encourage eligible households to apply before funding runs out. 
 By Valeria Aponte Feliciano • 
 Published November 2, 2026 • 
 Updated on November 2, 2026 at 11:26 pm 
 BOOKMARKER 
 Pennsylvania residents struggling with heating bills this winter could qualify for up to $2,000 in financial assistance through a state program that is now accepting applications .
 Applications are open for the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program, or LIHEAP, which helps eligible households pay their heating bills.

 With rising energy costs putting additional pressure on household budgets, Patricia King, PECO's manager of community engagement, expects more families to seek assistance this year.
 "We really hope that they do because there are a lot of families that do not apply," King said.
 Both renters and homeowners can qualify for LIHEAP, even if they're not behind on their heating bills. Eligibility is based on household size and income.
 Eligible households can receive up to $1,000 in heating assistance, plus an additional $1,000 if they experience a heating emergency.
 How to apply for LIHEAP in Pennsylvania

 The fastest way to apply for heating assistance is online through Pennsylvania's COMPASS website .
 Residents can also submit a paper application.
 Even if you received LIHEAP assistance last year, you must submit a new application to receive benefits this season.
 "If you have applications that you saved, LIHEAP applications from last year, throw them away. They will not be accepted," King said.
 When is the LIHEAP application deadline?
 The application period runs through April 23, 2027, but funding is limited, and residents are encouraged to apply as soon as possible.
 "We always encourage customers to apply as soon as the program opens because you want to make sure that you get the funding while funding is still available," King said.
 That means eligible households shouldn't wait until their heating bills become difficult to manage before seeking assistance.
 A new report said that the cost of heating your home will rise faster than inflation this winter, and an expert who spoke with NBC10 Responds' Valeria Aponte Feliciano shared ways that people can start preparing now. 
 Who qualifies for LIHEAP?
 Eligibility for Pennsylvania's LIHEAP program depends on household income and the number of people living in the home.
 Both homeowners and renters may qualify, and applicants do not need to have overdue heating bills to receive assistance.
 King encourages residents to check their eligibility even if they aren't sure they meet the requirements.
 Many people who could benefit from the program may not realize they're eligible.
 Residents can learn more about the program and submit an application through the state's COMPASS website .
